paper_title: Role of Molecular Weight on the Mechanical Device Properties of Organic Polymer Solar Cells

knowledge_points.content: The cohesive energy (Gc) of the P3HT:PC60BM bulk heterojunction layer ranges from ~0.5 to ~17 J/m², with higher values directly correlated to an increase in the molecular weight of the rr-P3HT polymer.
knowledge_points.evidence: Cohesive values ranged from ~0.5 to ~17 J m⁻², following the general trend of greater cohesion with increasing molecular weight.

knowledge_points.content: Increased mechanical cohesion in high molecular weight rr-P3HT is attributed to enhanced plasticity, driven by interchain pi-pi stacking, a higher density of tie molecules bridging crystalline domains, and increased polymer chain entanglements.
knowledge_points.evidence: For rr-P3HT, increased plasticity is realized through interchain π-π stacking for the crystalline segments... more interlamellar amorphous regions with chain folds and tie molecules allow for polymer chain entanglements which would increase frictional molecular pullout during cohesive failure.

knowledge_points.content: For rr-P3HT with a molecular weight ≥ 53 kDa, the cohesive energy of the active layer increases with film thickness because the plastic zone at the crack tip can expand to a larger volume before being constrained by the rigid glass substrates.
knowledge_points.evidence: By increasing the thickness of the BHJ layer, the plastic zone surrounding the crack tip in the BHJ layer can expand to a larger volume before being constrained by the stiff top and bottom glass substrates.

knowledge_points.content: Four-point bend (FPB) testing of organic solar cells with high molecular weight P3HT (≥ 53 kDa) reveals sawtooth-like features in load vs. displacement plots, indicating a time-dependent viscoelastic relaxation and stick-slip crack propagation.
knowledge_points.evidence: The more pronounced sawtooth-like features in the load vs displacement plot (Figure 1b) for OSCs made with ≥ 53 kDa rr-P3HT are indicative of a time-dependent viscoelastic relaxation process at the crack tip.

knowledge_points.content: Mechanical failure in P3HT:PC60BM solar cells is predominantly cohesive, occurring within the bulk heterojunction layer rather than at the interfaces, as confirmed by XPS analysis showing an elemental composition of ~90% C, ~8% S, and ~2% O on the fracture surfaces.
knowledge_points.evidence: For all devices, mechanical failure occurred within the BHJ layer as confirmed by elemental analysis of the cohesive surfaces with X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) which revealed an elemental composition of ~90% C, ~8% S and ~2% O.

knowledge_points.content: The storage modulus (E') of P3HT:PC60BM films measured by nanodynamic mechanical analysis (nDMA) ranges from 14 to 16 GPa, with lower molecular weight variants showing a slightly higher modulus due to higher crystallinity.
knowledge_points.evidence: From Figure 2, we see that for all Mw BHJ layers E' is ~14-16 GPa... it is interesting to note the increase in storage modulus as we decrease the Mw of rrP3HT. This may be indicative of the more crystalline nature of lower Mw rr-P3HT.

knowledge_points.content: A trade-off exists between mechanical robustness and electrical performance; the highest power conversion efficiency (PCE) is observed in lower molecular weight P3HT devices, whereas higher molecular weight increases cohesion but can reduce PCE due to morphological traps and paracrystallinity.
knowledge_points.evidence: A maximum PCE value was observed for the lowest rr-P3HT Mw. This has been attributed to morphological traps of charge carriers due to increasing paracrystalinity with increasing Mw... the most mechanically robust OSCs did not necessarily correspond to the most efficient.

knowledge_points.content: The optimal bulk heterojunction (BHJ) thickness for P3HT:PC60BM solar cells to maximize PCE is between 60 nm and 100 nm; exceeding this thickness increases mechanical cohesion but decreases efficiency due to increased charge carrier recombination.
knowledge_points.evidence: The maximum PCE corresponded to BHJ layer thicknesses between ~60 and 100 nm for these devices. As BHJ layers are made thicker, an increase in cohesion was observed (> 28 kDa) but with a steady decrease in PCE. This is due to a sharply declining short-circuit current (Jsc).

knowledge_points.content: Organic solar cell technologies with cohesive or adhesive energy values below 5 J/m² are considered difficult to manufacture at scale because low mechanical stability reduces production yield.
knowledge_points.evidence: studies have shown that device technologies with relatively low cohesive/adhesive energy (< 5 J m⁻²) become difficult to produce as mechanical failures can reduce production yield.

knowledge_points.content: Post-fracture surface analysis via AFM reveals that high molecular weight P3HT (100 kDa) results in high surface roughness (Rq ~46.7 nm) due to extensive plastic deformation and polymer chain pullout, whereas low molecular weight P3HT results in smooth fracture surfaces.
knowledge_points.evidence: By imaging the cohesive surfaces with optical microscopy (Figure 3a) and atomic force microscopy (AFM) (Figure 3b), we see significant differences in surface topography due to plastic deformation... OSCs made with low-Mw rr-P3HT produced relatively smooth, featureless cohesive surfaces.
